approved_by: Jason 2026-10-28 ("Can we determine what a good week will look like and what a bad week will look like ... trade bigger on good days, smaller on bad")
written_before: any per-bucket result. Known before: SC-FUT-0005 is right-skewed (best 20 days = 76% of profit) and stronger in volatile years (by-year table in the independent review).
question: Does anything known before the open tell SC-FUT-0005's good days from its bad days well enough that sizing up/down on it improves profit per contract out of sample?
strategy: workbench trial 266777ef (SC-FUT-0005, MNQ, practice 2019-05..2024-12), net of L3 costs, 1 contract; luck = mean of the matched random-direction control draws per day

predictors.vol: today's 14-prior-true-range sum ranked against the previous 250 sessions' values (min 60): low (< 1/3), mid, high (> 2/3)
predictors.streak5: the strategy's own net P&L over the previous 5 sessions: > 0 / <= 0

not_included: CPI / jobs-report days (need the FRED key; added later as a separate addendum) and the overnight gap (needs a data rebuild)
selection_on_train: for each predictor, the best and worst bucket by mean net $/day; pick the ONE predictor with the largest t-statistic of (best - worst)

rules.tilt: contracts x 1.5 in the best bucket, x 0.5 in the worst, x 1 otherwise; rescaled so the average weight over train days is 1 (same average size as untilted)
rules.skip: contracts x 0 in the worst bucket, x 1 otherwise; rescaled the same way

test.measure: improvement = mean(weight x net) - mean(net) per day on test days, and the change in daily Sharpe
test.gate: one-sided permutation p < 0.05: bucket labels shuffled across test days 5,000 times (seed 20261028); both rules reported (2 trials)
test.sanity: the same weights applied to the luck series should show no improvement

next_if_pass: a frozen prop-simulator run of P4 with the day weights; nothing traded on this result alone
